title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from pp. 3-5. Grothendieck is building an algebraic model of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid S0T_{0,I}. He defines it as the fundamental groupoid of the space PU_{0,I}, restricted to a finite set u(I) of base points. He has noticed that PU_{0,I} is a torsor under the compact torus U^I, where U is the circle group. He wants a description that uses only the exact sequence (S_I) 0→Z^I→R^I→U^I→0 and the torsor structure.

General setting (end of p. 3, top of this page). Take an extension of topological groups (6) 0→π→T̃→T→0, with T connected abelian, T̃ a finite-dimensional real vector space and π a free Z-module of finite type (a lattice). So T is a torus times a vector group and T̃→T is its universal covering.

Canonical fundamental groupoid. Let P be a U-torsor (written 𝒰). For x,y∈P there is a canonical bijection (7) Π(x,y) = Ũ_{y−x}, the fibre of the universal cover over the difference y−x∈U. Composition in Π(P) is addition in Ũ. Topologically this is correct. A path from x to y in P is x+γ(t), where γ is a path in U from 0 to y−x. Homotopy classes of such paths are exactly the lifts of y−x to Ũ, and concatenation corresponds to addition.

Abstraction. The formula makes sense for any extension of groups (8) 0→π→Σ→γ→0 together with a γ-torsor ε. One gets a connected 'π-groupoid' Σ(ε). Its objects are ε, with Hom(x,y)=Σ_{y−x}, the fibre of Σ→γ over the element sending x to y. Composition is the group law of Σ. Every vertex group is canonically identified with π, giving a groupoid with abelian band π. Equivalently (10): the set of arrows is Σ×ε, with source pr_2, target (u,x)↦u·x (Σ acting through γ), and composition (u,y)∘(v,x)=(uv,x). In other words Σ(ε) is the action groupoid of Σ acting on ε through its quotient γ.

Next page. Base change: for a morphism of torsors ε'→ε over γ'→γ, the induced π-groupoid on ε' is Σ'(ε'), where Σ' is the pulled-back extension. Application: S0T_{0,I} ≅ Σ_I(ω(I)) as Z^I-groupoids, for an extension Σ_I of a finite group by Z^I.

The margin seems to note the converse. Data (γ, γ-torsor, extension) should correspond to connected π-groupoids, at least in the connected case, presumably as an equivalence of categories.

Purpose: replace the topological fundamental groupoid by a purely group-theoretic object attached to a lattice extension and a torsor. These pieces can then be glued into the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical error. The hypotheses (T̃ a vector space, π a lattice, π in the identity component) are exactly what is needed for T̃→T to be the universal cover, so the identification Π(x,y)=T̃_{y−x} holds.

The 'π-groupoid' structure on Σ(ε) canonically identifies all vertex groups with π. Strictly, this needs π abelian, or more generally needs one to work with a band (lien) rather than with π itself. This is implicit; the page treats the abelian case first.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a torsor under a connected abelian Lie group (torus × vector group): Π(x,y) = fibre of the universal cover over y−x, composition by addition
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid of a torsor / of a torus via its universal covering

ideas.what: Groupoid Σ(ε) from an extension 0→π→Σ→γ→0 and a γ-torsor ε: objects ε, Hom(x,y)=Σ_{y−x}, arrows Σ×ε
ideas.modern_name: action (translation) groupoid Σ⋉ε, a connected groupoid with band π
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Brown's groupoid methods, Giraud (bands/gerbes)

ideas.what: Margin hint that connected π-groupoids correspond to (group γ, γ-torsor, extension of γ by π)
ideas.modern_name: classification of connected groupoids by vertex group plus object set; groupoids with abelian band ↔ extensions

ideas.what: Use of this to give an algebraic model of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid on a finite set of base points (S0T_{0,I} ≅ Σ_I(ω(I)), next page)
ideas.modern_name: genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid with tangential/combinatorial base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); later developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (the Teichmüller tower, base points) — only in general form, not with this torus-torsor construction

missed.claim: This is an early, explicit technical step towards the Teichmüller groupoid of the Esquisse. The genus-0 groupoid on a set of base points is realised as the fundamental groupoid of a torus torsor (PU_{0,I} as a U^I-torsor). This is then encoded algebraically by a lattice extension acting on a torsor. Such a torus-torsor model of S0T_{0,I} does not appear in the published Esquisse. The construction itself is elementary, however.
missed.quote: (7) Π(x,y) = Ũ_{y−x} (fibre de Ũ en y−x∈U) ... pour toute extension de groupes abéliens (8) 0→π→Σ→γ→0 et un torseur ε sous γ - on trouve un π-groupoïde connexe Σ(ε)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest. It documents how Grothendieck intended to define the base-point Teichmüller groupoids combinatorially from circle/torus torsors attached to stable curves, possibly reflecting a 'tangential base point' viewpoint.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard covering-space and groupoid folklore: the fundamental groupoid of a torus torsor, and the action groupoid of an extension. It is interesting only as context for Grothendieck's construction of Teichmüller groupoids, which is itself known from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely '(commutatifs), T̃ est un espace vectoriel réel de dim. finie, π un Z-module libre de t.f.' rather than 'espace contractile'.
Line 3-4: likely 'quels sont donc la topologie, et un groupoïde fondamental? On va décrire de façon purement algébrique le groupoïde. On trouve, pour x,y∈P, une bijection canonique'.
Line with (8): likely 'pour toute extension de groupes abéliens'.

In (8)-(10) the letters are Σ (the extension), γ (the group) and ε (the torsor), consistent with the next page. So: '0→π→Σ→γ→0', 'torseur ε sous γ', 'π-groupoïde connexe Σ(ε), ayant ε comme ensemble de ses objets', 'Hom(x,y)=Σ_{y−x}', 'addition dans Σ'.
(10) should read 'Fl Σ(ε) = Σ × ε' (source pr_2, as on the next page).
Margin, very uncertain: something like 'Ainsi on trouve une équivalence entre catégories des triples (groupes γ, γ-torseurs, extensions) et π-groupoïdes connexes (cas abéliens?)'.
